perspective:
From Vincent Chinana’s subjective perspective, he has access to:

- He knows he is a mechanic, and that Patrick Guzman is his long-time friend since their teenage years; they share blue-collar work and often collaborate, combining Vincent’s mechanical skills with Patrick’s construction expertise.
- At the diner, Vincent hears Patrick say he is considering a new construction venture to expand his business. Patrick thinks it is worth the risk but is still weighing options. Vincent tells Patrick he has heard it is risky, worries about financial security, and suggests reconsidering or delaying until Patrick gathers more information. Patrick thanks him and says he will think it over.
- Later, at Patrick’s construction site, Vincent notices Patrick avoiding detailed discussion about the investment. Vincent tells Patrick he feels Patrick is not telling him everything and that, as his friend, he feels betrayed by the lack of transparency. Patrick says it is complicated, that he did not want to worry Vincent with details, apologizes, says he should have been more open, and agrees to sit down and explain everything.
- At Vincent’s garage, Vincent learns the situation is serious. Patrick tells him it has been tough and that he might lose a significant amount if it does not turn around soon. Vincent offers to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses. Patrick gratefully accepts Vincent’s support.
- At the coffee shop, Vincent becomes aware—and says—that the venture might actually turn a profit after all. Patrick says it is starting to look up and that he is relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologizes for doubting him earlier and proposes a joint venture. Patrick agrees to work out the details.
- At Vincent’s house, Vincent is optimistic. He says their combined skills can make the venture a success and that they should start drafting a business plan, outlining every step carefully. Patrick agrees and emphasizes covering all their bases.

Vincent does not have access to Patrick’s private thoughts, hidden events, or information Patrick did not disclose to him.
